source: Written 2026-10-17 from the verified oracle text (Scryfall via carddb --verify, fetched 2026-10-17) for every card a scene shows or names, Scryfall's rulings (Tom, Bert, and William; Avacyn, Angel of Horror; Ghalta, Primal Hunger; Gray Merchant of Asphodel; Twilight Diviner; Ayara, First of Locthwain; Woe Strider; Part in Friendship; Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest; Fleshbag Marauder; Ilysian Caryatid; Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma; Archfiend of Despair; Archfiend of Depravity; Villainous Wrath, Carrion Feeder, Sol Ring, Grave Titan, Yargle, Glutton of Urborg, Gigantic Big Bear, Carnage Tyrant and Saber-Tooth Moose-Lion have none published) and this deck's notes. Cards a caption names are [[bracketed]] so clips.py checks them against the current list. Opponents' cards are placeholders, never named. Power and toughness are Scryfall's printed values, matching the Power column of the collection attrs file (Tom, Bert, and William 5/5, Avacyn 8/8, Ghalta 12/12, Gigantic Big Bear 10/7, Yargle 9/3, Carnage Tyrant 7/6, Saber-Tooth Moose-Lion 7/7, Mazirek 2/2, Archfiend of Despair 6/6, Archfiend of Depravity 5/4, Gray Merchant 2/4); Yargle has no rules text at all, and the 2/2 Zombies are Grave Titan's oracle text. Stipulated, not dealt: the Wrath's target controls five creatures (clip 3); Part in Friendship's first creature card is Grave Titan, with nine lands out (clip 4, an example, since the reveal is random); no opponent has lost life yet (clip 5). Scenes with Avacyn on the battlefield carry no turn number on purpose: this deck's notes record that the goldfish cast her by turn 10 in only 3% of 4,000 games, so no clip implies she arrives early. Ilysian Caryatid makes two mana of one color while you control a creature with power 4 or greater (oracle text). Commander starting life is 40 (CR 903.7). Dies means put into a graveyard from the battlefield (CR 700.4), which is where a sacrificed permanent goes (CR 701.21a); exile isn't dying. The commander's, Carrion Feeder's and Woe Strider's costs have no tap symbol, so they can be activated whenever you have priority (CR 117.1b), an opponent's turn included. Clip 1: Ghalta's reduction can't take it below {G}{G}, its total cost is locked in as you cast it, and its mana value stays 12 (rulings; CR 601.2f), which is why Part in Friendship sends it to your hand (clip 4). Tom, Bert, and William use the sacrificed creature's power as it last existed on the battlefield (ruling). Only the active player discards to hand size in the cleanup step (CR 514.1). A return created during an end step waits for the next turn's end step (CR 513.2), so the body is sacrificed before the end step. A player who attempted to draw from an empty library loses (CR 704.5b). Avacyn's trigger creates a delayed triggered ability that you control (CR 603.7, 603.7e) and that exists independently of her (CR 113.7a); if she dies with other nontoken creatures, she triggers for each, herself included (ruling; CR 603.10a). Tokens: Avacyn's text says nontoken, and a token that has left the battlefield can't come back (CR 111.8). Devotion counts the black mana symbols in the mana costs of your permanents (CR 700.5), artifacts included, counted as the drain resolves, the Merchant itself included (rulings): the returned artifact commander still adds its {B}. A token copy has the original's mana cost (CR 707.2) and its enter abilities trigger (Twilight Diviner ruling); it is a black creature entering, so Ayara triggers for it too. You order your own simultaneous triggers (CR 603.3b), and the last one put on the stack resolves first (CR 405.5). Clip 2: devotion 12 = Avacyn 3, Ayara 3, Merchant 2, copy 2, Diviner 1, Woe Strider 1; two drains of 12 and Ayara's 1 twice make 26 per opponent. Clip 3: the commander's return has an intervening if (CR 603.4), so a death as an artifact doesn't trigger it; the return finds the card in the graveyard (CR 400.7e); moving a commander to the command zone is an optional state-based action (CR 903.9a), performed before triggers go on the stack (CR 117.5); a recast from the command zone pays commander tax (CR 903.8). Avacyn's trigger for the commander does nothing at end step, since the card already left the graveyard as a new object (CR 603.7c, 400.7). Devotion 6 = Avacyn 3, Merchant 2, the artifact commander 1; the Caryatid's {1}{G} has no {B}. Clip 4: Mazirek's ability looks back in time (CR 603.10a) and triggers once for each permanent sacrificed (CR 603.2c; ruling), and Fleshbag Marauder's sacrifices all happen at once, Fleshbag itself allowed (rulings), so four players' sacrifices are four triggers; a creature sacrificed to pay the commander's cost triggers Mazirek, and that trigger resolves before the draw (ruling), as does Part in Friendship's, both put on the stack above the ability (CR 117.5, 603.3); Part in Friendship triggers only once each turn (oracle text). Clip 5: devotion 9 = Avacyn 3, Archfiend 2, Merchant 2, Diviner 1, commander 1, then 11 with the copy; 40 - 9 - 11 - 11 = 9, and the Archfiend takes the 31 lost that turn again, to -22. Archfiend of Despair counts only life lost, as its trigger resolves (rulings); a player at 0 or less life loses (CR 704.5a), and a player whose opponents have all left the game wins (CR 104.2a). Archfiend of Depravity: the opponent chooses as it resolves, without targeting, and may spare fewer than two (rulings).

scenes.head: Tom, Bert, and William: power into cards
scenes.sub: A 5/5 for {3}{B}{G}. {1}, sacrifice another creature: draw cards equal to its power, then discard a card.
scenes.say: Tom, Bert, and William. Pay one and sacrifice another creature: draw cards equal to its power, then discard one.

scenes.head: [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger]]: the biggest body
scenes.sub: A 12/12 trampler for {10}{G}{G}. It costs {X} less, where X is the total power of creatures you control. Never less than {G}{G}.
scenes.say: Ghalta, Primal Hunger: a twelve-twelve that costs X less, X being your creatures' total power. Never less than two green.

scenes.head: Your turn: 13 power on board, so Ghalta costs {G}{G}
scenes.sub: Avacyn's 8 power and the commander's 5 take off all ten generic: two Forests cast Ghalta.
scenes.say: Your turn, with Avacyn and the commander out. Her eight power and their five take off all ten generic, so two Forests cast Ghalta.

scenes.head: Their turn: {1}, sacrifice Ghalta, draw 12
scenes.sub: On the next opponent's turn, a Swamp you left untapped pays {1}. Ghalta had 12 power: draw 12, then discard a card. Avacyn triggers.
scenes.say: On the next opponent's turn, a Swamp you left untapped pays one. Sacrifice Ghalta: twelve power, so draw twelve, then discard one. Avacyn triggers.

scenes.head: Their end step: Ghalta returns
scenes.sub: Avacyn returns it at the beginning of their end step. Only the active player discards to seven at cleanup, so the cards wait for your turn.
scenes.say: At their end step, Avacyn returns Ghalta. Only the player whose turn it is discards down to seven, so the cards wait for your turn.

scenes.head: Again, on every opponent's turn
scenes.sub: Sacrifice it before each end step: 12 more cards, and it's back at that end step.
scenes.say: Do it again on every opponent's turn. Sacrifice it before their end step: twelve more cards, and it's back at that end step.

scenes.head: Mind your library
scenes.sub: Twelve on every turn is 48 cards a round. A player who has to draw from an empty library loses, so stop when it runs low.
scenes.say: Mind your library. Twelve on every turn is forty-eight cards a round, and drawing from an empty library loses the game. Stop when it runs low.

scenes.head: Every big body is a big draw
scenes.sub: [[Gigantic Big Bear]] draws 10, [[Yargle, Glutton of Urborg|Yargle]] 9, [[Carnage Tyrant]] and [[Saber-Tooth Moose-Lion]] 7. [[Goreclaw, Terror of Qal Sisma|Goreclaw]] makes each cost {2} less.
scenes.say: Every big body is a big draw: Gigantic Big Bear ten, Yargle nine, Carnage Tyrant and the Moose-Lion seven. Goreclaw makes each cost two less.

scenes.head: Avacyn, Angel of Horror
scenes.sub: An 8/8 deathtouch flier for {5}{B}{B}{B}. Whenever she or another nontoken creature you control dies, it returns at the beginning of the next end step.
scenes.say: Avacyn, Angel of Horror. Whenever she or another nontoken creature of yours dies, it comes back at the beginning of the next end step.

scenes.head: With Avacyn out, sacrifice [[Gray Merchant of Asphodel|Gray Merchant]]
scenes.sub: [[Woe Strider]] does it for no mana: scry 1. The Merchant died, so Avacyn triggers. [[Ayara, First of Locthwain|Ayara]] and [[Twilight Diviner]] are out too.
scenes.say: With Avacyn, Ayara and Twilight Diviner out, Woe Strider sacrifices Gray Merchant for no mana and scries one. A sacrifice is a death: Avacyn triggers.

scenes.head: End step: the Merchant returns from your graveyard
scenes.sub: Its drain, [[Ayara, First of Locthwain|Ayara]] and [[Twilight Diviner]] all trigger, in the order you choose. Put Diviner's on top: it resolves first.
scenes.say: At the end step, the Merchant returns from your graveyard. Its drain, Ayara and Twilight Diviner all trigger, in your order: put Diviner's on top.

scenes.head: Diviner copies it: a second Merchant
scenes.sub: It entered from a graveyard, so Diviner makes a token copy, once each turn. The copy has the Merchant's {3}{B}{B}. Its drain and Ayara trigger too.
scenes.say: It entered from a graveyard, so Diviner makes a token copy. The copy has the Merchant's mana cost, and its own drain and Ayara trigger too.

scenes.head: Devotion to black: 12, twice
scenes.sub: Avacyn 3, Ayara 3, Merchant 2, copy 2, Diviner 1, Strider 1. Two drains of 12, plus Ayara's 1 twice: each opponent loses 26.
scenes.say: Count the black symbols in your permanents' mana costs: twelve, the copy included. Two drains of twelve, and Ayara's one, twice: each opponent loses twenty-six.

scenes.head: Tokens never come back
scenes.sub: Avacyn's text says nontoken: sacrifice the copy and it's gone for good. Keep it, and its {B}{B} adds 2 to every later drain.
scenes.say: Tokens never come back: Avacyn says nontoken. Sacrifice the copy and it's gone for good. Keep it, and it adds two to every later drain.

scenes.head: Every turn, not just yours
scenes.sub: Free outlets like [[Carrion Feeder]] work at instant speed. Sacrifice the Merchant before each opponent's end step, and it drains again at that end step.
scenes.say: Every turn, not just yours. Free outlets like Carrion Feeder work at instant speed: sacrifice the Merchant before each opponent's end step, and it drains again.

scenes.head: Tom, Bert, and William can't stay dead
scenes.sub: If they die as a creature, they return to the battlefield right away, as an artifact. They're no longer a creature.
scenes.say: Tom, Bert, and William can't stay dead. If they die as a creature, they return right away, as an artifact. They're no longer a creature.

scenes.head: [[Villainous Wrath]]: a drain, then a wipe
scenes.sub: A {3}{B}{B} sorcery. Target opponent loses life equal to the number of creatures they control. Then destroy all creatures.
scenes.say: Villainous Wrath. Target opponent loses a life for each creature they control, then all creatures are destroyed.

scenes.head: Your turn: cast it with Avacyn out
scenes.sub: [[Sol Ring]], a Swamp and [[Ilysian Caryatid]] pay {3}{B}{B}: with a 4-power creature out, the Caryatid makes two. The target opponent loses 5.
scenes.say: Your turn, with Avacyn out. Sol Ring, a Swamp and Ilysian Caryatid pay: with a four-power creature out, the Caryatid makes two. The target opponent loses five.

scenes.head: Everything dies. The commander comes straight back
scenes.sub: Decline the command zone: it's optional. Their own trigger returns them right away, as an artifact. The rest wait for Avacyn.
scenes.say: Everything dies. Decline the command zone, since it's optional, and the commander's own trigger returns them right away, as an artifact. The rest wait for Avacyn.

scenes.head: An artifact now, so the outlet stays
scenes.sub: Removal and wipes that hit only creatures can't touch it. It works the same: {1}, sacrifice another creature, draw.
scenes.say: An artifact now, so the outlet stays: removal that hits only creatures can't touch it. And it works the same: pay one, sacrifice another creature, draw.

scenes.head: End step: order the returns, the Merchant's first
scenes.sub: Avacyn triggered for each of your nontoken creatures, herself included. Put the Merchant's return on the stack first: it resolves last.
scenes.say: At the end step, order the returns: Avacyn triggered for each of your nontoken creatures, herself included. Put the Merchant's first, so it resolves last.

scenes.head: Only your side comes back
scenes.sub: Avacyn and the Caryatid return, then the Merchant: devotion 6, with Avacyn 3, Merchant 2 and the artifact commander's {B}. Their creatures stay dead.
scenes.say: Only your side comes back. Avacyn and the Caryatid return, then the Merchant drains six: Avacyn three, Merchant two, and the artifact commander one.

scenes.head: The catch: artifact removal and exile
scenes.sub: Destroyed as an artifact, they weren't a creature, so they don't return. Exile isn't dying either. Then it's the command zone, and commander tax.
scenes.say: The catch: destroyed as an artifact, they weren't a creature, so they don't come back. Exile isn't dying either: then it's the command zone, and tax.

scenes.head: [[Part in Friendship]]
scenes.sub: Once each turn, when a nontoken creature of yours dies, reveal until a creature card. Mana value at most your land count: it enters. Higher: to your hand.
scenes.say: Part in Friendship. Once a turn, when your nontoken creature dies, reveal until a creature. It enters if its mana value is at most your land count.

scenes.head: [[Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest]]
scenes.sub: A 2/2 flier for {3}{B}{G}. Whenever a player sacrifices another permanent, put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control. Any player, any permanent.
scenes.say: Mazirek, Kraul Death Priest. Whenever any player sacrifices another permanent, put a +1/+1 counter on each creature you control.

scenes.head: Turn 9: sacrifice the Goat first
scenes.sub: [[Yargle, Glutton of Urborg|Yargle]], a vanilla 9/3, is out. [[Woe Strider]] sacrifices its Goat for free: Mazirek puts a counter on each of your creatures. Yargle is 10/4.
scenes.say: Turn nine. Woe Strider sacrifices its Goat for free, and Mazirek puts a counter on each of your creatures. Yargle, a vanilla nine-three, is now ten-four.

scenes.head: {1}, sacrifice Yargle: draw 10
scenes.sub: Its power as it left was 10. The sacrifice triggers Mazirek again, and Yargle was nontoken, so Part in Friendship triggers too. Both resolve before the draw.
scenes.say: Pay one and sacrifice Yargle: ten power as it left, so draw ten. Mazirek and Part in Friendship both trigger, and resolve before the draw.

scenes.head: Friendship's trigger on top: say it finds [[Grave Titan]]
scenes.sub: Mana value 6, nine lands: it enters, with two 2/2 Zombies. Then Mazirek's counter goes on all of them, and then you draw 10.
scenes.say: Friendship's trigger on top. Say it finds Grave Titan: mana value six, nine lands, so it enters with two Zombies. Then Mazirek's counters, then the draw.

scenes.head: Every player's sacrifice counts
scenes.sub: [[Fleshbag Marauder]]: each player sacrifices a creature. You and three opponents make four sacrifices: four counters on each creature you control.
scenes.say: Every player's sacrifice counts. Fleshbag Marauder makes each player sacrifice a creature: with three opponents, four sacrifices, and four counters on each creature you control.

scenes.head: Once each turn, on every turn
scenes.sub: Let a nontoken creature die on each opponent's turn too. A reveal over your land count, like [[Ghalta, Primal Hunger|Ghalta]] at 12, goes to your hand instead.
scenes.say: Once each turn: let a nontoken creature die on opponents' turns too. A reveal over your land count, like Ghalta at twelve, goes to hand.

scenes.head: [[Archfiend of Despair]]: the loss, twice
scenes.sub: A 6/6 flier for {6}{B}{B}. Opponents can't gain life, and at each end step, each opponent loses again the life they lost this turn.
scenes.say: Archfiend of Despair. Your opponents can't gain life, and at the beginning of each end step, each opponent loses the life they lost that turn, again.

scenes.head: [[Archfiend of Depravity]]: they keep two creatures
scenes.sub: A 5/4 flier for {3}{B}{B}. At each opponent's end step, that player chooses up to two creatures they control, then sacrifices the rest.
scenes.say: Archfiend of Depravity. At each opponent's end step, that player keeps up to two creatures and sacrifices the rest.

scenes.head: Each opponent at 40: cast [[Gray Merchant of Asphodel|Gray Merchant]]
scenes.sub: Your turn. Avacyn, the Archfiend, [[Twilight Diviner]] and the commander are out. [[Sol Ring]], [[Ilysian Caryatid]] and a Swamp pay {3}{B}{B}.
scenes.say: Your turn, each opponent at forty. Avacyn, the Archfiend, Twilight Diviner and the commander are out. Sol Ring, the Caryatid and a Swamp cast Gray Merchant.

scenes.head: Devotion 9: each opponent drops to 31
scenes.sub: Avacyn 3, Archfiend 2, Merchant 2, Diviner 1, commander 1. It was cast from your hand, so Diviner doesn't copy it.
scenes.say: Devotion is nine: Avacyn three, the Archfiend two, the Merchant two, Diviner and the commander one each. Each opponent drops to thirty-one.

scenes.head: {1}: sacrifice it to the commander, draw 2
scenes.sub: The Merchant's 2 power: draw two, discard one. It died, so Avacyn returns it at the beginning of your end step.
scenes.say: Pay one and sacrifice the Merchant to the commander: two power, so draw two, discard one. Avacyn returns it at your end step.

scenes.head: End step: the Archfiend's trigger goes on the stack first
scenes.sub: It triggers with Avacyn's return, and you choose the order. First on the stack resolves last: after every drain.
scenes.say: At your end step, the Archfiend's trigger and Avacyn's return trigger together. Put the Archfiend's on the stack first: it resolves last, after every drain.

scenes.head: The Merchant returns, and Diviner copies it
scenes.sub: Diviner's trigger on top, so both drains count 11: the copy adds 2. Each opponent goes from 31 to 9.
scenes.say: The Merchant returns from your graveyard, and Diviner copies it. With Diviner's trigger on top, both drains count eleven: each opponent goes from thirty-one to nine.

scenes.head: Then the Archfiend: 31 more
scenes.sub: Each opponent lost 31 this turn, so each loses 31 again: from 9 to −22. All three lose, from 40, in one turn.
scenes.say: Then the Archfiend's trigger resolves. Each opponent lost thirty-one this turn, so each loses thirty-one again: minus twenty-two. All three lose, from forty, in one turn.
